title: Centennial Bell (Independence Hall)
status_note: Strikes the hours with a mechanical hammer since 1926.

place.label: Tower of Independence Hall, Philadelphia
place.coords_source: OpenStreetMap Nominatim lookup of the named site (ODbL)

maker: Meneely-Kimberly foundry, Troy, New York; gift of Henry Seybert
mass_note: 13,000 lb, 1,000 lb for each of the original 13 states (NPS)

alloy.note: bell bronze; contains metal from four melted cannons (NPS)

timeline.event: Cast at Meneely-Kimberly, Troy, for the centennial
First rings for the nation's 100th birthday; listeners find the tone poor
Sent back to Troy and recast; in the steeple again by the end of 1876
A mechanical hammer begins striking the hours

tiers.everyday: The Centennial Bell hangs where the Liberty Bell once did, in the Independence Hall tower. It weighs 13,000 lb and rings every hour.
tiers.student: NPS gives 13,000 lb and a 7 ft 6 in diameter, cast at Meneely-Kimberly in Troy in 1876. Its metal includes 400 lb from four cannons: one American and one British from Saratoga, one Union and one Confederate from Gettysburg (fact sheet). Since 1926 a hammer strikes it on the hour. The National Register form gives 7 ft 3/4 in across (conflict kept open).

model.label: Parametric profile scaled from the sourced diameter; the curve itself is a generic Western bell profile, not a scan.
